Subject: Request: Custom SLA Exhibit for Redwood Order Form

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — we liked the latency profiles and the routing options. Legal and procurement at MedioSys have reviewed the baseline order form and we're going to need a custom SLA exhibit to match our enterprise requirements before procurement can advance. High-level asks from IT and Legal: 

- Availability guarantee: 99.95% monthly uptime for production endpoints (we understand Dedicated offering can make this simpler).
- Latency: P90 under 350ms for text-generation endpoints (we can scope model families rather than specific model IDs).
- Data residency: logs and telemetry stored in us-east-1; audit logs retained 13 months.
- Incident notification: 2-hour initial acknowledgement for Sev 1, and full RCA within 10 business days.
- Remedies: service credits up to 25% of monthly fee for repeated SLA misses (Procurement wants explicit calculation examples).

Attaching a spreadsheet with the exact clauses Legal wants redlined. Can you confirm whether Redwood will: (1) accept the proposed uptime figure with the proposed remedies, (2) provide an exhibit we can attach to our MSA, and (3) if anything requires Dedicated or Private deployment (we are evaluating both)?

Also looping in Jack (IT lead) and will share procurement contact after I get your initial take. Let us know if you'd like to do a quick call this week to run through the asks.

Best,
Christina
Christina Park
Head of Procurement — MedioSys

- Latency: We can commit to P90 under 350ms for the targeted model family (we'll list the model variants and maximum sequence lengths in the exhibit).
- Data residency & audit logs: Supported in our Private and VPC deployments; for Hosted we can guarantee storage region and 13-month retention in most cases (we'll include an evidence table).
- Incident notifications & RCA: We can offer 2-hour ack for Sev1 and 10 business day RCA for enterprise tiers; we'll add escalation contact details.
- Remedies: We typically provide tiered service credits; we'll include worked examples for calculation and propose a 20% cap for recurring breaches with carve-outs for Force Majeure and customer-side misconfigurations.

I'll draft an SLA exhibit and share an initial redline. Ben, can you help confirm whether the 99.95% commitment requires Dedicated capacity in our standard contract language and what operational exceptions we should call out?

From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.ai>

Internal summary / proposed approach:

1) Availability: For 99.95% we recommend (a) Dedicated reserved pool scoped to the customer's production environment OR (b) Hosted with guaranteed reserved throughput (higher commit). We should include an "Availability Measurement" section (how we calculate downtime, maintenance windows, scheduled maintenance notice period).

2) Exceptions: carve out scheduled maintenance (72-hour advance notice for planned maintenance windows >2 hours), customer-induced outages (misuse, DDoS if not routed through our protected endpoints), third-party outages (cloud provider).

3) Remedies: propose monthly service credit equal to (outage minutes / total minutes) * monthly fee * 0.5 but capped at 20% for each incident and 25% aggregate per month. Procurement asked for a worked example — I can mock one.

4) Latency: P90 commitment to be scoped by model family and max sequence length; for >2k tokens we may not guarantee 350ms, call out sequence length tiers.

5) Evidence & Logs: provide proof of compliance via audit logs and token-level latency histograms. For Hosted we can provide a redacted dataset of traces monthly; for Private we'll provide full audit log access per KMS policy.

6) RCAs and notifications: 2-hour ack for Sev1; updates every 4 hours until mitigated; RCA within 10 business days.

7) Order form language: include an Exhibit A (Service Levels) and a Schedule X (Availability Measurement & Remedies). We can add a clause that allows Redwood to propose mitigation (traffic reroute to other region) subject to customer approval for data residency-sensitive traffic.

Attachments: Redwood_Orderform_TrackChanges.pdf (I'll attach a tracked-changes PDF with our suggestions).

Action items:
- Laura: can you provide legal redline on the Remedies cap and Force Majeure language?
- Stephanie: ops — confirm deployment constraints and whether 99.95% is operationally achievable on Hosted with reserved pools vs Dedicated.
- Priya: I'll draft a worked example for the credit calculation and a crisp paragraph for the Exhibit.

Ben

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-26T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Re: Request: Custom SLA Exhibit for Redwood Order Form

Thanks — quick legal comments inline.

- Remedies cap: we should aim for a 20% monthly cap rather than 25%; 25% aggregate could be acceptable only with additional indemnity carve-outs. Procurement teams push hard here; propose 20% with an escalator clause after 12 months if performance is good.

- Measurement: Be explicit about the measurement window (calendar month) and what constitutes "unavailable" (API 5xx responses + inability to get a health-check token). Also add a clause that cache warming / model loading time is excluded for cold-start events if they occur after model upgrades.

- Force Majeure: Keep standard language but add an explicit callout for "widespread cloud provider outage" as a carve-out.

- Data residency: For Hosted promises, say "geographic residency controls" rather than absolute guarantee — unless customer signs for Private deployment.

- Service credits: include worked examples and require notice of claim within 30 days of the month in question.

I'll produce a tracked redline of Redwood_SLA_Exhibit_v1.docx and the orderform PDF.

Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference

Hi Christina — apologies for the short delay. We discussed your request with Legal and Ops and attached an SLA exhibit with our proposed language and redlines to your spreadsheet. Highlights: 

- Availability: Redwood is prepared to contractually commit to 99.95% monthly uptime for production endpoints when the customer opts for Dedicated reserved capacity, or for Hosted + Reserved Commitments with defined throughput tiers. We include an "Availability Measurement" section and scheduled maintenance windows.

- Latency: P90 < 350ms will be scoped to the model family and maximum sequence length; we include a table of supported models and sequence tiers in the exhibit.

- Remedies: we propose the following credit model (worked examples in the exhibit): monthly credit = (outage minutes / total minutes in month) * monthly fee * 0.5; per-incident cap 20%; monthly aggregate cap 20%; claims to be submitted within 30 days. Laura has suggested limiting the aggregate to 20% and adding standard FML carve-outs.

- Data residency: for Hosted we will guarantee storage in the requested region and 13-month log retention; absolute residency guarantees require Private deployment.

- Notifications & RCA: 2-hour ack for Sev1, updates every 4 hours until mitigation, RCA within 10 business days.

Attached: "Redwood_SLA_Exhibit_v1.docx" (tracked changes) and "Redwood_Orderform_TrackChanges.pdf". If the changes look good to you, we can prepare a DocuSign-ready Exhibit A to attach to your MSA and route it through procurement.

2) If acceptable, confirm whether MedioSys prefers Dedicated or Hosted+Reserved Commitments in the order form so we can finalize operational parameters.
3) We'll prepare the DocuSign packet once legal signs off.
